items.title: Section: Which Elements Span All Three Realms, Which Are Grasped by Life, and Their Scriptural Synonyms

items.zh: 問：幾唯色無色界繫？答：無。問：幾通三界繫？答：三。問：幾執受？幾非執受？答：五執受，五執受、非執受，所餘一向非執受。何以故？以離於彼，餘能執受執受於彼不可得故。云何種種界？謂即十八界展轉異相性。云何非一界？謂即彼諸界無量有情種種差別所依住性。云何無量界？謂總彼二名無量界。如佛世尊，於惡叉聚喻中說：我於諸界，終不宣說界有邊際。
items.en: Question: how many span all three realms? Answer: three. Question: how many are appropriated, and how many are not? Answer: five are always appropriated; five are sometimes appropriated and sometimes not; the rest are never appropriated. What are manifold elements? The eighteen elements each displaying their own mutually distinct character. What is not a single element? These same elements serving as the basis for countless beings' boundless variety. What are measureless elements? The combination of both. As the World-Honoured One said in the Akṣa-Cluster Simile Discourse: regarding the elements, I would never declare any final limit.

items.zh: 中嗢拕南曰：何等、實有性、四句、與同分、取、界、執受非、種種等非一。

items.title: Section: Six Meanings of "Element" — And Why Even Nirvāṇa and Space Earn the Name

items.zh: 問：何等是界義？答：因義、種子義、本性義、種性義、微細義、任持義是界義。問：以何義故，涅槃、虛空亦說名界？答：由彼能持苦不生義，持身眼等運動用義。
items.en: Question: what is the meaning of "element"? Answer: the meaning of cause, of seed, of inherent nature, of lineage, of subtlety, and of sustaining. Question: for what reason are nirvāṇa and space also called elements? Answer: because they sustain suffering's own permanent non-arising, and sustain the functioning of the body's limbs and eyes in motion.

items.title: Section: Why Eighteen Specifically, and Six Further Ways of Slicing the Same Elements

items.zh: 問：為顯何義建立界耶？答：為顯因緣義及顯根境受用義。問：此十八界由誰分別？答：若略說當知由六種：一、法界。謂眼等法有眼等界。二、淨界。謂住種性補特伽羅所有諸界。三、本性界。謂即如所說十八界，無始時來，於後後生其性成就；及住種性、不住種性補特伽羅，無始時來，涅槃、非涅槃法其性成就。四、熏習界。謂即此諸界，淨不淨法先所熏習，於生死中得勝劣生涅槃因性。五、已與果界。謂即此諸界，感果已滅。六、未與果界。謂即此諸界，未感得果，或滅、未滅。如是略說諸界有六種；若廣說者，其數無量。
items.en: Answer: because attaining nirvāṇa grants a cool, unshakeable freedom, no longer subject to the three realms' own painful result, nirvāṇa sustains suffering's own non-arising, hence "element." Because space exists, the eye can perceive form and the body can move; space sustains bodily motion and the eye's own perception, hence "element" as well. Question: for what purpose are the elements established? Answer: to reveal the causal relationship, and the functional relationship between faculty, object, and experience. Question: by what is this classified? Answer: briefly, by six: elements as phenomena, pure elements, elements as inherent nature, elements as habituation, elements already yielding their result, and elements not yet yielding their result. This is only a brief summary; the actual number is without limit.

items.zh: 問：此十八界，幾有色？幾無色？乃至幾無斷耶？答：如前所說相應隨順建立。

items.title: Section: Does the Eye Really See? Ultimate Truth Says No, Conventional Truth Says Yes

items.zh: 問：如說眼見諸色乃至意了諸法，此為眼等是見者乃至是了者耶？為彼識耶？答：約勝義道理，非是眼等，亦非彼識。何以故？諸法自性眾緣生故，剎那滅故，無作用故。約世俗道理，眼等最勝，故可於彼立見者等。
items.en: Question: when it is said the eye sees form, up through mind understanding phenomena, are the faculties themselves what see or understand, or their corresponding consciousnesses? Answer: in the ultimate sense, neither the faculties nor those consciousnesses. Why? Because all phenomena arise from manifold conditions, cease the very instant they arise, and possess no genuine function. In the conventional sense, the faculties are the most prominent factor, and so it is proper to speak of them as the ones that see and so on.

items.zh: 何以故？若有眼等諸根，識決定生。無所缺減，或有識流；非眼等根若缺不缺，俱可得故。

items.title: Section: Sequence at Last — Why the Eye Is Named First, and the Buddha's Three Ways of Teaching

items.zh: 此中實義，唯於見等說見者等。問：此十八界，幾種次第宣說因緣？此復何等？答：略有二種。一、三種次第宣說因緣，二、六種次第宣說因緣。云何三種次第宣說因緣？謂所依、境界、俱依差別故。所以者何？由識與根同一處義，故說名依；境界是所緣義，故亦名依。云何六種次第宣說因緣？謂彼所行眾多差別數數行故，先說眼等。是初因緣。又隨世間俗事轉故，說彼次第。由諸世間先互相見，次相慰問，次設飲食，次過晝分夜分現前，敷設種種軟妙臥具氈褥被枕，觸習侍女。是第二因緣。又喜樂差別為依止故，次第宣說。是第三因緣。
items.en: The genuine meaning here is that it is only with respect to seeing and the rest that one speaks of a "seer" and the rest. Question: by how many kinds of sequence are the eighteen elements explained? Answer: briefly two — a threefold scheme and a sixfold scheme. Because the eye's own scope of activity is by far the greatest and most frequent, it is named first — this is the first reason. Because it follows the natural sequence of ordinary social life — this is the second reason. Because it follows the varying degree of pleasure each provides — this is the third reason.

blocks.text: A famous question: does the eye see? Ultimately no one sees; conventionally, the eye is foremost.
Master Cháng Bǎi: form on which feeling can arise is "appropriated" form. The elements' distinct characters make them "manifold"; their serving countless beings makes them "not single".

Cause, seed, inherent nature, lineage, subtlety, and sustaining. Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 is "cause" since it can give rise to all things. Nirvāṇa and space are called elements in the sense of sustaining: nirvāṇa sustains the non-arising of suffering; space lets the body move.
They reveal causal relation and the relation of faculty to object. Master Cháng Bǎi: the uncontaminated seeds of the three vehicles are "pure elements".

"Ultimately neither the faculties nor the consciousnesses see, since things arise from conditions, cease at once, and have no function; conventionally the faculties are foremost." Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from seeing, there is no seer; it is not "I" seeing, but faculties and consciousness at work.
Six reasons, beginning with how much and how often each faculty acts.
"It is not 'I' seeing." Try noticing this the next time you look at something: seeing happens, and the "I" is added afterwards.

quiz.q: Among the eighteen, how many are only of the desire realm, of desire and form, and of all three?
options: desire realm only, eleven; desire and form, four; all three, three, form above being scarce
desire realm only, three; desire and form, four; all three, eleven
form only, eleven; formless only, three; desire, four
desire realm only, four; desire and form, eleven; all three, three
quiz.why: The treatise gives four, eleven, and three. Master Cháng Bǎi: smell, taste, and nose- and tongue-consciousness exist only in the desire realm, since only there is solid food; taking away those four and the three spanning all realms leaves eleven for desire and form: the five faculties, three consciousnesses, and three objects.

quiz.q: The English has "how many are grasped by life" for 幾執受. How does the lecture explain 執受?
options: 執受 is being gripped by life, all things having life, so "by life" is exact, mountains and rivers included
form on which rebirth depends is 執受; what adheres to the body is appropriated, and objects apart from it not; "by life" narrows it
執受 is holding something by hand
執受 is taking precepts
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: form on which rebirth depends is what 執受 means; if feeling can arise depending on this form, it is called appropriated; the five objects adhering to the body are appropriated, and those apart from the faculties are not. The English "grasped by life" obscures the relation to consciousness, and §62 of fascicle 53 uses "appropriated."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain manifold, not-single, and measureless elements?
options: manifold means many worlds, not-single worlds beyond earth, and measureless a boundless cosmos, all about spatial size
界 is seed; differing natures of seeds are manifold; differing seeds give countless beings of the ten realms
all refer to kinds of hell
all refer to realms of supernormal power
quiz.why: The treatise defines manifold elements as the eighteen's mutually distinct character, not-single as their serving as the basis for countless beings, and measureless as both. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings are provisional and elements real; 界 is seed; on differing seeds, countless beings of the ten dharma-realms arise.

quiz.q: What are the six meanings of element?
options: accumulation, intermixture, summary, increase, decrease, and means, the same as aggregate under another name
cause, seed, inherent nature, lineage, subtlety, and sustaining
growth, gate, means, combination, support, and dwelling
earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness
quiz.why: The treatise gives cause, seed, inherent nature, lineage, subtlety, and sustaining. Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 is called cause since it can give rise to all phenomena and serve as their basis; what has manifested through practice is coarse, while what is still seed is subtle. The English "potential for realisation" drops the lineage sense of 種性.

quiz.q: Why are nirvāṇa and space also called elements?
options: because nirvāṇa and space are seeds generating all things, wholly like the eye-element, real causes
because both have location
nirvāṇa sustains suffering's non-arising; space sustains the movement of body and eyes
because both are produced by karma
quiz.why: The treatise answers by the sustaining sense: nirvāṇa sustains the non-arising of suffering, and space the functioning of body and eye. Master Cháng Bǎi: space sustains bodily movement and lets the eye see form, and so too is called an element. The two sentences opening §40 in the English are the lecturer's paraphrase, not treatise text.

quiz.q: For what purpose are the elements established, and how does this relate to the six meanings?
options: to reveal causal relation and the use of faculty and object; these are the seed and sustaining meanings
to reveal selflessness and nirvāṇa; these are the nature and lineage meanings, so elements and aggregates differ in aim
to reveal the world's size; this is the subtlety meaning
to reveal retribution; this is the cause meaning
quiz.why: The treatise answers that the elements reveal the causal relation and the functional relation of faculty and object. Master Cháng Bǎi: of the six meanings, the eighteen elements here take only seed and sustaining; the seed meaning is the causal relation, and the sustaining meaning is the use of faculty and object.

quiz.q: By which six are the eighteen elements briefly classified?
options: of the three realms, contaminated, uncontaminated, and unconditioned, by realm and contamination
the six elements of earth through consciousness
elements as phenomena, pure, of inherent nature, of habituation, having yielded, and not yet yielded
the six faculties
quiz.why: The treatise lists six. Master Cháng Bǎi: the elements of beings abiding in the uncontaminated lineage of the three vehicles are pure elements; newly infused uncontaminated seeds having the causal nature for nirvāṇa are elements of habituation. The definitions themselves are missing from the English, which keeps only the names.

quiz.q: "The eye sees forms": how does the treatise speak ultimately and conventionally?
options: ultimately the eye truly sees and consciousness truly knows; conventionally nothing is seen, the conventional being false
ultimately neither faculty nor consciousness, for things arise from conditions, cease at once, and have no function; conventionally the faculties are foremost, so are called seers
both say eye-consciousness sees
both say the self sees
quiz.why: The treatise says that ultimately neither the faculties nor the consciousnesses see, since phenomena arise from conditions, cease at once, and have no function; conventionally the faculties are foremost and may be called seers. Master Cháng Bǎi: in ultimate truth neither eye nor eye-consciousness sees; "the eye sees" is provisionally set up.

quiz.q: The English has "simply that seeing occurs, without positing any further seer." How does this differ from the Chinese emphasis?
options: the Chinese says a seer truly exists beyond seeing, so the English is wholly reversed
the Chinese says only a buddha is a seer
the Chinese says "seer" is spoken only of seeing, keeping the word; the English turns it into no seer; the lecture says no seer exists apart from seeing
the Chinese says the seer is eye-consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from seeing and the like, no other seer exists; seeing form and hearing sound is not an I doing so, but faculties and consciousnesses at work. The English reaches the right conclusion, but the Chinese makes a point about language: "seer" is said only of seeing itself. The English replaces that with a denial.

quiz.q: What are the first three reasons for the sequence of the elements?
options: abundance and frequency of activity; following worldly custom; depending on differences of pleasure
by the three realms, the three times, and the three moral qualities, all by doctrinal classification
by order of teaching, disciples' capacity, and length of sūtras
by strokes, alphabet, and rhyme
quiz.why: The treatise gives abundance and frequency of activity, following worldly custom, and differences of pleasure as the first three of six reasons. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the arrangement by the six faculties, the six objects they take, and the six consciousnesses that depend on them. The sequence reflects how experience is actually used, not a metaphysical order.
